rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, which this render never sees, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing. ply: 1 — the format version every rule below is read under; a version this build does not speak is refused, never guessed at

What this document declares. "0 functions promise nothing" counts functions that end up with nothing checked -- whether nobody wrote any checks for them, or the document switched checking off for them on purpose. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.

component cli — maps to Rust module ply_cli The library behind `cargo-ply`. Its shell -- argument parsing, file I/O, subprocess calls -- is deliberately unclaimed; what is claimed is the logic those commands share. declares checks up to fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — the strongest verdict this could earn if every declared check ran and passed; a promise, never a result this box is this shade because `join_plainly` is the weakest thing in it: it declares fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

component shared — maps to Rust module ply_cli::shared What `check`, `audit` and `worklist` all need from a document before any engine runs. One copy, so the three commands cannot quietly disagree about what they read. declares checks up to fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — the strongest verdict this could earn if every declared check ran and passed; a promise, never a result this box is this shade because `is_local` is the weakest thing in it: it declares fuzzed — checked against many random inputs — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

is_local fuzz(256) — tries 256 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result| *result == local_module_path(&local_anchors, &anchor).is_some() the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs

local_module_path fuzz(256) — tries 256 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures test — runs the declared examples plus generated cases; each case must satisfy the function's requires and ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result| !local_anchors.is_empty() || *result == Some(String::new()) the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs 3 worked examples — the `test` check above compiles each into a test when `cargo ply verify` runs; a promise of what will run, never a result

crate_root_fn_key fuzz(256) — tries 256 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures test — runs the declared examples plus generated cases; each case must satisfy the function's requires and ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result| result.ends_with(fn_key.as_str()) Postcondition (ensures): |result| module.is_empty() || result.starts_with(module.as_str()) the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs 2 worked examples — the `test` check above compiles each into a test when `cargo ply verify` runs; a promise of what will run, never a result

contract_text fuzz(256) — tries 256 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures test — runs the declared examples plus generated cases; each case must satisfy the function's requires and ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result| !result.is_empty() Postcondition (ensures): |result| requires.iter().all(|r| result.contains(r.as_str())) Postcondition (ensures): |result| ensures.iter().all(|e| result.contains(e.as_str())) the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs 2 worked examples — the `test` check above compiles each into a test when `cargo ply verify` runs; a promise of what will run, never a result

wrap fuzz(256) — tries 256 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures input and post contract: Postcondition (ensures): |result| text.split_whitespace().all(|w| result.contains(w)) the checks above are what will test the function against exactly this promise when `cargo ply verify` runs
